Subject: Post-call: Fastlane deploy-mode recommendation & pilot next steps

Thanks for a productive call earlier — quick recap and a recommended path so we can get a pilot standing up next week. High-level notes from our discovery:

- Workload: conversational search + re-ranking service. Typical sustained QPS ~250, daily peak bursts up to ~1,000 for promotions.
- Avg tokens per request: ~80 (prompt+response), median sequence length skews short but tail exists.
- SLO targets you gave: p95 <= 220ms, p99 <= 400ms (user-facing).
- Data residency/security: US only, no sensitive PHI.

Options we discussed (short):
1) Hosted API (fastest to market) – fits smaller steady-state workloads, benefits from automatic routing and prefix caching. Pros: no infra ops, quick onboarding. Cons: potential variability at very high sustained QPS unless reserved capacity added.
2) Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pool) – predictable throughput and isolation; recommended for sustained 250+ QPS with 1k bursts where p99 matters. Pros: deterministic latency, autoscaleable with burst controls. Cons: commit required, provisioning lead time.
3) Private VPC/on-prem – (likely unnecessary for Fastlane now) if you require full network isolation or on-prem hardware.

My recommendation: run a 2-week Dedicated pilot with an automated fallback to Hosted for overflow. That lets us validate p95/p99 under your real traffic while keeping availability guaranteed during unexpected spikes. To move forward I need three items from your side: a 24-48 hour sample traffic trace (anonymized), confirmation on target SLOs & retention policy, and sign-off on the attached pilot quote.

Attachments: fastlane_traffic_sample.csv (example format), pilot_quote_v1.pdf

Next steps (proposed):
- You: drop sample trace and confirm SLOs by EOD Monday.
- Us: provision pilot Dedicated pool (2x A100 equiv) + canary routing to Hosted; run baseline synthetic and then replay trace.
- 48 hrs after replay: joint review with perf graphs; decide go/no-go for production commit.

If this path looks good I’ll open the pilot ticket and loop in infra to start provisioning.

Thanks,

James — good questions. Quick answers and an engineered path:  

1) Ballpark costs (very rough, will finalize with your traffic trace):
- Hosted (reserved concurrency + caching): ~$1,800–2,400 per 1M tokens processed (depends on burst headroom and model variant); for your steady-state volumes estimate ~ $25k–35k/mo.
- Dedicated (reserved GPU pool with autoscale/burst): ~ $28k/mo fixed for the pilot (2x A100-equivalent), + incremental token compute when exceeding baseline. Dedicated becomes more cost-effective as sustained volume grows because unit GPU efficiency improves.

2) Performance: Hosted can meet p95 <= 220ms for shorter sequences if you accept higher cost and reserved capacity; p99 under bursty spikes is much more reliable on Dedicated because of node isolation and consistent batch scheduling. Our default approach for customers with your p99 needs is Dedicated pilot with canary Hosted overflow.

3) Data handling: Hosted does NOT use customer prompts/responses for model training by default for enterprise customers; we can enable data retention = "none" and route logs to your ingest only. I’ll attach our security summary in the pilot ticket.

Technical config we’d prototype in the pilot:
- Model variant: rw-v1.0-l (quantized) or rw-1.3c for lower latency budget.
- KV cache TTL: 30s for conversation reuse.
- Batching: adapt up to batch size 8 for Dedicated; Hosted uses dynamic batching.

Next steps: I’ll open the pilot order and send the DocuSign link for the quote. Ben will run a quick synthetic baseline (p50/p95/p99) and then replay your trace once we receive it. Marissa — can you own infra provisioning once the DocuSign is signed?
